proposals.title: Refresh the volunteer page from the Fall 2026 volunteer sheet
proposals.body:
## Summary

The user wants the /volunteer page brought in line with the "Fall 2026 | HIT Volunteer Opportunities" Google Sheet (Drive file 1YmLbinAVIhGYnJHKpy3B0aSpc7QpNoAZGggR0BcIJWc, tab "Fall 2026"). The sheet lists roles such as Alumni Volunteer Coordinator, City Volunteer and City Lead or Co-Lead (SF / Bay Area, Boston / Cambridge, NYC x AI Events), Founders Task Force volunteer and co-lead, and Editorial, each with a description and a point of contact. The site's volunteer projects live in the `projects` collection (`src/content/projects/*.md`) and render on /volunteer.

## Key Decisions

- Publish ROLES ONLY: title, description, and (if the user agrees) the point-of-contact name. Never publish the volunteer names, emails, phone numbers or availability columns the sheet also holds.
- One project entry per distinct role, not per "1 of ∞" row; the sheet repeats each role across rows.
- Confirm with the user which existing project entries (IG Content Creator, LinkedIn Engagement Specialist, Social Media Marketing Specialist, Writer) stay, merge, or retire.
- City lead/co-lead roles link naturally from the new "Lead or co-lead a chapter →" item in the Chapters menu, which already points at /volunteer.

## Implementation

1. Read the sheet's Fall 2026 tab and draft the role list for the user to confirm.
2. Add or update `src/content/projects/<role>.md` entries (title, blurb, active, dates, body), following the shape of `src/content/projects/ig-content-creator.md`.
3. Update the volunteer-page scenarios (`volunteer-page-open-projects`, `volunteer-page-no-open-projects`) and recapture after the content is committed.
proposals.reason: You asked for the volunteer opportunities to match your sheet; it was kept out of this change.

proposals.title: Seeded scenario captures break while site content is uncommitted
proposals.body:
## Summary

Scenario capture on this Astro site cannot produce trustworthy frames of SEEDED app scenarios while any file under `src/content/` or `src/data/` is uncommitted. The content sandbox (`initContentSandbox` in `astro.config.mjs`, `.codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox/`) does not engage, so seeds are refused ("served committed content"). The documented workaround of stashing those files for the capture pass also failed this session: it produced frames with the chapters and communities collections EMPTY (no Chapters menu group), and `recapture-stale` reported them as clean "Recaptured". Every content-changing feature therefore ends with seeded frames that must be restored by hand and force-recaptured after the commit.

## Key Decisions

- A capture whose seed or collections did not land must fail loudly, never report "Recaptured".
- The sandbox should seed from the WORKING TREE's `src/content` when it is dirty, rather than switching off, so content edits and seeded scenarios can be captured together before the commit.

## Implementation

1. In `astro.config.mjs` (`initContentSandbox`), seed the sandbox from the working-tree `src/content`/`src/data` when dirty, and never leave a collection directory empty across a dev-server restart (the empty-collection-dir watcher bug).
2. Add a post-capture assertion for seeded app scenarios: when a collection the page renders is empty but the seed or production content has rows, fail the capture.
3. Re-verify with `harvard-in-tech-phone-menu-open` and `webinars-route-the-surviving-recordings`, which both captured empty roster frames this session.
proposals.reason: Seeded full-page screenshots came out empty or wrong but were reported as captured.

proposals.title: Screenshot staleness misses data files the page reads at runtime
proposals.body:
## What happened

This feature changed only `src/data/nav.json` (plus a few code files). The site reads that file at runtime through `readSingleton('nav.json')` in `src/lib/site.ts`, not through an import, so the screenshot staleness hash never includes it. Two seeded /donate scenarios were captured with the old menu while nav.json was stashed (the stash was needed to get the seeded captures past the dirty-content guard), and afterwards `scenario-coverage`, the strict audit and `session-finalize` Phase 3.5 all reported them as fresh. The only way to find them was to eyeball the header of each frame, and fixing them needed `recapture-stale --force --target`.

## What would have helped

Include content/data files that pages read at runtime (`src/data/*.json`, `src/content/**`) in the render-input hash, at least for application scenarios on this stack, or let `stack.json` declare runtime-read data roots. A frame that shows stale data should read as stale.
proposals.reason: Frames showing the old menu were reported fresh because nav.json is not part of the staleness hash.

proposals.title: Syncing capture scripts marks every screenshot stale
proposals.body:
## What happened

At Verify Prototype, `client-errors` refused to run because `.codeyam/capture.js` predated the binary and said to run `sync-capture-scripts`. After the sync, `scenario-coverage` reported 229 of 293 scenarios stale with reason "capture pipeline changed". The full `recapture-stale` sweep took about 38 minutes, and 247 of its captures came back pixel-identical and were restored. None of that work was related to the feature.

## What would have helped

Treat a capture-script sync as a re-verify rather than a staleness event, or let the sync record the new pipeline version without invalidating frames until a capture actually differs. At minimum, have `client-errors` and `sync-capture-scripts` warn up front that the sync makes the whole corpus stale and roughly how long the sweep will take.
proposals.reason: One required script sync turned 229 untouched scenarios stale and cost a long full sweep that changed nothing.

proposals.title: Frame the past-events section in the two events-page scenarios

The scenarios `events-route-the-calendar-with-no-past-events-yet` and `events-route-upcoming-and-past` seed different event sets, but both capture only the top of `/events` (page banner plus the Luma calendar embed). The past-events listing where they differ sits below the visible area, so the two frames are byte-identical and `scenario-review` flags the pair as a seed-error candidate. Before this was noticed they only differed by whatever the live Luma widget happened to show.

## Key Decisions

- Add an `interactions` hover on the past-events heading to each scenario, so each capture frames the section that proves its state (URL fragments do not scroll captures).
- Do not mock or freeze the Luma embed here; framing past the embed avoids depending on its live content.

- `.codeyam/scenarios/events-route-the-calendar-with-no-past-events-yet.json` and `.codeyam/scenarios/events-route-upcoming-and-past.json`: add `"interactions": [{"action": "hover", "text": "<past events heading>"}]`, reading the heading from `src/components/EventsPage.astro`.
- Recapture both with `--force --target` and confirm the frames now differ.
proposals.reason: The 'no past events yet' and 'upcoming and past' events-page screenshots are identical, because the part that differs is below the visible area.

proposals.title: Give the chapter Sign up band a benefit-led pitch
proposals.body:
## Summary

Every chapter page carries two newsletter pitches. The global-community band's card now leads with what lands in the inbox ("Get the newsletter" — events, chapter news and alumni stories, local news first). The chapter's own "Stay in touch / Sign up" band (`src/components/ChapterSignUp.astro`) still reads "Join the Harvard Alumni in Tech community." with a bare "Subscribe" button, which says nothing about what a reader gets and repeats the ask without a reason. Rewrite that band so it pitches the chapter-local benefit — hearing about this city's events first — and so the two pitches on one page complement rather than echo each other.

## Key Decisions

- Keep the band and its Mailchimp link (`siteLinks().mailingList`, overridable via `subscribeUrl`); change wording only.
- Make it chapter-specific where possible (e.g. pass the city name so the intro can say "Hear about London events first"), since the global-community card already covers the general pitch.
- Do not add a subscriber count; that figure is hard-coded in several places already and drifts.
- Leave the header "Subscribe" button alone — it must stay one short word at 390px.

## Implementation

### 1. Rewrite the band copy

**File**: `src/components/ChapterSignUp.astro` (45 lines)

Update the `SectionHead` `kicker` / `title` / `intro` and the button label. If the copy names the city, add an optional `city` prop and pass it from `src/components/ChapterPage.astro`.

### 2. Keep fixtures and scenarios in step

Update `src/pages/isolated-components/ChapterSignUp.astro` and recapture the `ChapterSignUp - Default` scenario plus the chapter-page scenarios that show the band.
proposals.reason: Chapter pages now pitch the newsletter twice: the new benefit-led card, and a generic 'Sign up / Subscribe' band above it.

proposals.title: Seed check rejects a capture when the seeded value matches committed content
proposals.body:
## What happened

`recapture-stale` failed `events-route-the-calendar-with-no-past-events-yet` with `BLOCKED: the render ... showed "On March 20, 2018, Harvard in Tech hosted its second Crypto + Blockchain event..." where this scenario's own seed wrote "On March 20, 2018, Harvard in Tech hosted its second Crypto + Blockchain event..."` — the two strings are identical. The guard picks a field whose seeded value equals the committed value, so it cannot distinguish 'seed landed' from 'seed missed' and reports a false failure. A rerun of the same capture later passed.

## What would have helped

Only use a field as seed evidence when its seeded value differs from the committed value; when no such field exists, skip the check (or say it was inconclusive) instead of blocking.
proposals.reason: A capture was refused as 'reading committed content' when the seed's text was word-for-word the committed text.

## Summary

Community pages reuse ChapterEvents, whose empty state is built from the page's subject as a place: `No events scheduled in ${name} yet.` For a city that reads well ("in London"); for a community it reads oddly ("in Investors", "in AI"). The heading was already overridden for communities (`Upcoming ${name} Events`), but the empty line was not. Seen on the new Investors page capture (community-route-investors-join-steps).

## Key Decisions

- Keep ChapterEvents shared; add an optional override for the empty-state title, the same way `heading` is overridden.
- Community wording: "No Investors events scheduled yet."
- Also reconcile the AI On Day One scenario description, which says the events section renders nothing when empty; the current pages render a heading plus an empty-state box.

## Implementation

1. `src/components/ChapterEvents.astro` (empty state near line 57): accept an optional `emptyTitle` prop, defaulting to the current place wording.
2. `src/components/CommunityPage.astro` (line 99): pass `emptyTitle={`No ${name} events scheduled yet.`}`.
3. Recapture the community route scenarios and update the AI On Day One description to match what renders.
proposals.reason: A community with no events reads 'No events scheduled in Investors yet', phrasing built for a city.

proposals.title: Show a compact subscribe card when the Luma calendar has nothing upcoming
proposals.body:
## Summary

The events page embeds Luma's calendar in a fixed-height frame (`src/components/LumaCalendar.astro`, `height: clamp(340px, 46vh, 540px)`). When nothing is upcoming, Luma fills that frame with its own grey "No Upcoming Events" panel, so on a phone the page shows a big, mostly empty box — the decision sheet row `m-calendar-box`, still open after the October responsive check (`docs/responsive-check-2026-10.md`, item O1). We cannot restyle inside Luma's frame, and its panel also sits ~36px inside our column on the right.

## Key Decisions

- Decide on the build side, not in the browser: the nightly-imported events collection already knows whether anything is upcoming.
- When nothing is upcoming, render the existing branded `luma-card` ("Browse & subscribe on Luma") instead of the iframe; when something is, keep the embed.
- Owner call: confirm this is wanted before building — it changes what the events page shows on quiet weeks.

## Implementation

1. `src/pages/events.astro`: compute whether the events collection has any future-dated entry and pass it to `LumaCalendar`.
2. `src/components/LumaCalendar.astro`: add a prop (e.g. `hasUpcoming`) and render the card branch when it is false even if `embedUrl` is set.
3. Scenarios: events page with and without upcoming events at Mobile, so both branches are on record.
4. Re-run `npm run check:responsive -- --only /events`.
proposals.reason: On /events the Luma embed is a large, mostly empty grey box whenever no event is scheduled (decision sheet m-calendar-box).

proposals.title: Demo gate treats a scroll-only hover from preview-interact as the demo interaction
proposals.body:
## What happened

While verifying layout I used `preview-interact` with `hover` on `.dots` purely to scroll the carousel into view. At Prepare Demo, `advance` refused: "the recorded interaction (hover \".dots\") produced NO observable DOM change … the control itself is inert" — even though a verified capture and attestation existed. It took a preview-flow with a real Menu click to clear it, and the flow's text-matching click on "Menu" first failed because the button also holds an icon.

## What would have helped

Only count interactions recorded at the Demo step (or explicitly marked as the demo), and let a hover used for scrolling be declared as such. A `click` text match that tolerates an icon inside the button would have saved one failed run.
proposals.reason: A hover used only to scroll a band into view for checking later blocked the Demo step as an 'inert control'.

The `momentum-fund-the-donor-wall-moved-to-the-top` scenario (`.codeyam/scenarios/momentum-fund-the-donor-wall-moved-to-the-top.json`) seeds 19 donors and four `momentumSections` with the recognition band at order 4. On current code the live preview of that scenario shows the plain 'Let's go further together.' hero with no network, and the committed screenshot was refreshed to match on 2026-10-14. Nothing in that session touched the donate page, so this predates it.

## Key Decisions

- Decide whether the recomposition (recognition band as hero) is still wanted. If yes, fix the page; if it was deliberately retired, rewrite the scenario's description to match.

## Implementation

1. Read `src/pages/donate.astro`, `src/components/MomentumFundPage.astro` and `src/components/donate/MomentumNetwork.astro` for the condition that promotes the recognition band to the hero.
2. Compare with the scenario's seed (donors, momentumSections) to find which condition no longer holds.
3. Fix the condition or update the scenario description, then recapture `momentum-fund-the-donor-wall-moved-to-the-top` and compare with `momentum-fund-public-visitor`, which still shows the network.

proposals.title: Give EventCard its own glossary entry
proposals.body:
## Summary

`src/components/EventCard.astro` renders every event card (home page, chapter pages, /events) and was reshaped on 2026-10-14 into one square-image card shape, but it has no glossary entry, so coverage tools cannot plan states for it (`scenario-coverage-plan generate --component EventCard` errors) and it is only covered indirectly through `EventCardGrid` scenarios.

## Key Decisions

- Cover it with its own component scenarios rather than relying on the grid.

## Implementation

1. Isolate `EventCard` and add states: upcoming with cover and Learn more link, past with cover, no cover (H-mark stand-in), long title clamped to two lines, no location.
2. Register the scenarios and add the glossary entry citing them.
proposals.reason: EventCard (src/components/EventCard.astro) renders every event card on the site but has no glossary entry.

proposals.title: Generated isolation pages fail the type check for components with required props
proposals.body:
## What happened

`codeyam-editor editor isolate BannerCta` generated `src/pages/isolated-components/BannerCta/[...state].astro` with `const props = scenarios[name] ?? {};` and `<Component {...props} />`. Because the props module types `scenarios` as `Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>`, and `BannerCta` requires `href` and `label`, `verify-build` failed at the App Scenarios step with `ts(2322): Type '{}' is not assignable to type 'IntrinsicAttributes & Props'`. The fix was re-running `isolate --force --content` with a hand-edited body that casts the props to the component's shape.

## What would have helped

Generate the page with the props typed from the component (e.g. `ComponentProps<typeof Component>`) or fall back to `scenarios.Default` with a cast, so a component with required props type-checks out of the box.
proposals.reason: A freshly isolated component with required props broke astro-check until the page was hand-rewritten.

proposals.title: scenario-coverage-plan generate aborts on a component with no glossary entry

## What happened

## What would have helped

proposals.title: A dead session's plan claim blocks the audit and nothing in the editor can release it
proposals.body:
## What happened

At the Reconcile step the audit failed on `SELECTED_PLAN_NOT_IN_COMPLETED` for a plan this session never touched (`remove-or-repurpose-the-unused-chapter-volunteer-link-field`). Its claim ref had been written by a session that started at 19:06 and died at once: `lastHeartbeatAt` equalled `startedAt`, the pid was gone, and there was no transcript. The finding says the claim is 'owned by this worktree' and its fixCommand archives the plan into `completed/`, which would falsely record unbuilt work as shipped.

There is no editor command to release a stale claim. Deleting the local ref did not help: the claim-sync task re-fetched it from origin within seconds. Deleting it on origin was refused by the editor's own hook (`git push is only allowed at slug(s): push`), and the harness's permission classifier also refused it as destructive. In the end the user had to run the delete by hand, and two attempts failed first because a long ref name wrapped when pasted.

## What would have helped

- A `plan-claim-release <slug>` (or `--reap-dead`) command that verifies the owning pid is dead or the heartbeat is frozen, then deletes the ref locally and on origin in one step.
- The audit finding distinguishing 'claim from a dead session' from 'archive lost on a live claim', and suggesting the release instead of the archive in the first case.
proposals.reason: Saving was blocked for several turns; the user had to delete a git ref on GitHub by hand.

proposals.title: Auto-registered renamed tests lose their descriptions
proposals.body:
## What happened

I rewrote three tests in `src/lib/presenceConsistency.test.ts`, which changed their names, and ran `refresh-tests --force`. Afterwards the registry had replaced the three old entries with the new keys but set each `description` to an empty string, even though every `it()` has a `//` comment above it. Then `rename-test` refused because the new keys were 'already in the registry'. The blanking only showed up in `git diff .codeyam/test-registry.json`; I fixed it with three `register-test` upserts.

## What would have helped

- Carry the old entry's description across when a removed key and an added key share a file and line, which is the case `LIKELY_RENAME_DETECTED` already spots, or derive it from the source comment as `reconcile-registry` does.
- Print a warning whenever an auto-registration writes an empty description.
proposals.reason: Three renamed tests landed in the registry with empty descriptions and had to be re-described by hand.

proposals.title: Registry reconcile deletes table-generated test entries
proposals.body:
## What happened

`reconcile-registry --auto-apply` removed all eight `it.each` rows from `src/lib/selectOptions.test.ts` (`enum-shaped fields are dropdowns, not text boxes › <coll>.<field> is a select` and `existing content still validates against the new dropdowns › every committed <coll>.<field> value is offered`), although the tests still exist and pass. After restoring them with `register-test-batch` (which refuses `it.each` cases until given an explicit `line`), they disappeared AGAIN before the Reconcile step, and the audit then failed with `RUNNER_HAS_UNREGISTERED_TEST` for the same eight keys. A dry-run `reconcile-registry` reported nothing to add, so the audit and the reconcile disagreed about the same rows.

## What would have helped

Reconcile treating loop-generated test names (resolved from the runner's own output) as present rather than orphaned, and never removing a row whose key the runner still emits. Failing that, `register-test-batch` resolving `it.each` cases to the generator line by itself.
proposals.reason: The 8 it.each dropdown tests in selectOptions.test.ts vanished from the registry twice and failed the audit until re-registered by hand.

proposals.title: Editor preview proxy stopped answering after a dev-server double launch
proposals.body:
## What happened

After `dev-server '{"action":"restart"}'` launched two `astro dev` trees, I killed the non-managed tree by PID. Later the reverse proxy on :4321 stopped answering (`restart-dev-server` reported a proxy-only wedge with the app healthy on :4322), every capture failed its pre-flight, and the only fix offered was `restart-server`, which needs user approval because it can end the session. The in-place re-exec then left the app dev server stopped, so a separate `dev-server start` was needed.

## What would have helped

A command that restarts just the reverse proxy, and `restart-server` bringing the app dev server back up after its re-exec.
proposals.reason: Captures and the Live Preview were dead until the editor itself was restarted, which needed the user's approval.

proposals.title: Preview captures cannot take a full-page screenshot
proposals.body:
## What happened

The user asked about sections far down the DC page. `preview` and `preview-verify` only return the viewport, and a `fullPage` field was silently ignored, so I wrote a throwaway Playwright script to screenshot the whole page.

## What would have helped

A supported `fullPage: true` option on `preview` / `preview-verify` (or a `capture-page` command) that saves the whole scrolled page.
proposals.reason: To check sections below the fold I had to hand-roll a Playwright script.

proposals.title: isolate scaffolds duplicate routes for hand-written isolation pages
proposals.body:
## What happened

At Isolation Routes, `isolate FormingChapterCta ChapterPage` generated `src/pages/isolated-components/FormingChapterCta/[...state].astro` and `ChapterPage/[...state].astro` plus `.codeyam/isolation-props/*.ts`, even though this project already serves those components from tracked hand-written pages (`FormingChapterCta.astro`, `[name].astro` with `ChapterPage-Forming`). The new folder would have shadowed the existing route, so I deleted the scaffolds by hand.

## What would have helped

`isolate` detecting an existing route that already serves the component's registered scenarios and doing nothing, or asking for `--adopt-existing`.
proposals.reason: It created FormingChapterCta/ and ChapterPage/ route folders that collided with the project's existing hand-written pages.
